findings: F1: 770 of 5,908 CNS5 rows have no Gaia G/BP-RP, including alpha Cen AB (CNS5:3627, 4.32 ly), Sirius (CNS5:1676), Procyon (CNS5:1895), Altair (CNS5:4912); under the quorum rule they render invisible. CNS5 carries a HIP column, so an exact id match is available.

F2: CNS5 has one 'Gl 559 AB' row (HIP 71683, 754.81 mas, 4.321 ly). HIP2 I/311 (fetched 2026-10-02): A 754.81+-4.11 mas, B (HIP 71681) 796.92+-25.90 mas = 4.09 ly. D-17's 4.365 ly (Kervella 2016, 747.17 mas) is in no shipped catalogue.
F3: the design doc's >60 s Python fallback and the planned Python stats/audit tools conflict with the Python policy (#34); stats and audit move to Godot headless, AC2/AC3/AC11 commands amended.

F4: forward CMB at the cap is a sky-filling glow (3,853.7 K ahead HB-63, 1,926.9 K at 90 deg); needs absolute photopic radiance in the package because surfaceBrightnessRatio(2.725 K, D) divides by ~0.

F5 (CORRECTED 2026-10-02): sideways (apparent theta'=90 deg) the sky is REDSHIFTED, D = 1/(gamma(1 - beta cos theta')) = 1/gamma (0.141 at 0.99c); blueshift only within 29.8 deg of forward at 0.99c. D-6 'goes dark sideways' is correct physics; Q5 withdrawn. The earlier F5 used a ship-frame angle in the rest-frame formula.

F6: stars.json (CNS3) feeds starfield, galaxy map, names.json (index-keyed), test_physics, test_galaxy_map, sim/core_test doubles, record_godot_session, replay goldens alpha_cen/godot_map_voyage and the destar mask: the switch is its own milestone (M1.7).

F7: PR #43/#36 is a dependency for M1.2d (AILANG fixed-width parser) and M1.7 (AILANG destar); N1/N2 were already closed in T2 (PR #19), remaining T1/T2 residuals are N3, tier-name validation, safe squared-distance range and the real-row F32 bound.
